lessons.objective: Translate verbal rules, apply the order of operations and simplify products and fractions.

Evaluate brackets, then indices, then products or divisions, then sums or differences.

A product of two brackets has four products before collecting like terms.

examples.title: Evaluate in the right order
examples.question:
For a lamp circuit, the value of \(x\) is 5.

  1. Evaluate \(1+2x^2\).

    [2]

  2. Explain why adding first gives a different result.

    [1]
examples.solution:
(a) Square 5 first to get 25.

Multiply by 2, then add 1.

\(51\)

(b) The index acts on \(x\) before the coefficient is used.

The operation order keeps the constant separate.

examples.title: Expand a double bracket
examples.question:
A rectangle has sides \(x+2\) and \(x+2\) units.

  1. Expand the expression for its area.

    [2]

  2. State the constant term.

    [1]

examples.title: Simplify a variable fraction
examples.question:
Take a non-zero value of \(x\). Consider \(\frac{14x^{9}}{2x^7}\).

  1. Simplify the fraction.

    [2]

  2. Explain the restriction on x.

    [1]

(a) Divide the numerical factors first.

(b) Simplification cannot make an undefined division valid.

The original denominator would be zero when \(x=0\).

examples.title: Reverse a formula

The rule is \(T=kn\). The variables are positive. For this case, \(k=5\) and \(T=10\).

  1. Find the value of \(n\).

An art club charges 2 tokens once, then 5 tokens per session. The bill is 17 tokens.

  1. Find how many sessions were booked.

    [2]

  2. Write the equation you used, with n for the number of sessions.

    [1]
examples.solution:

examples.title: Clear a variable denominator
examples.question:
Consider the equation \(\frac{36}{x+2}=9\) for real x.

  1. Find \(x\).

    [2]

  2. State the value excluded before solving.

    [1]
examples.solution:

Divide by 9, then subtract 2.

\(2\)

(b) This value makes the denominator zero.

\(x=-2\)

examples.title: Represent a cooling limit
examples.question:
A device starts at 26 degrees. Its temperature falls by 4 degrees each minute. It works only while the temperature is at least 2 degrees.

  1. For how many whole minutes can the device keep working?

    [2]

  2. Write the original comparison and solve it for t.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) \(26-4t\geq 2\).

After subtracting 26, divide by -4. Reverse the inequality sign.

\(6\)

(b) When dividing by a negative number, the direction changes.

\(26-4t\geq 2\), so \(t\leq 6\).

examples.title: Find rounding limits
examples.question:
The recorded reading is 1,120, rounded to the nearest 10 units.

  1. Give the lower limit.

    [2]

  2. Give the upper limit and say if it is included.

    [2]
examples.solution:
(a) Half a rounding step is \(5\).

\(1120-5=1115\).

\(1115\)

(b) \(1120+5=1125\). At this boundary the reading rounds up.

\(1125\), excluded.

examples.title: Match both conditions
examples.question:
Solve \(2x+y=12\) and \(3x+y=17\) together.

  1. Give the solution as an ordered pair (x, y).

    [2]

  2. Check your ordered pair in both conditions.

    [1]
examples.solution:
(a) Subtract the first equation from the second. The y terms cancel.

\(x=17-12=5\).

Put this value back into either equation.

\((5,2)\)

(b) Substitute the two values together and check both totals.

Both conditions are true.

examples.title: Match both conditions
examples.question:
Two lines have equations \(y=2x-11\) and \(y=-x+10\).

  1. Give the intersection as an ordered pair (x, y).

    [2]

  2. Check your ordered pair in both conditions.

    [1]
examples.solution:
(a) At an intersection, both equations give the same y-value.

\(2x-11=-x+10\).

Solving gives x = 7. Then y = 3.

\((7,3)\)

(b) Substitute the two values together and check both totals.

Both conditions are true.

examples.title: Match both conditions
examples.question:
At a plant sale, 14 plants are sold. A herb costs 2 credits and a flower costs 3 credits. The total is 33 credits.

  1. Give an ordered pair (herbs, flowers).

    [2]

  2. Check your ordered pair in both conditions.

    [1]
examples.solution:
(a) If x is herbs and y is flowers then \(x+y=14\) and \(2x+3y=33\).

Double the first equation and subtract it from the second. That gives y.

Put y = 5 into the first equation to find x.

\((9,5)\)

(b) Substitute the two values together and check both totals.

Both conditions are true.
